BOTH DONE AND PUSHED.

    #2006  BUG-1297   ad13bb0ec7   5206 passed, 0 failed
    #2014  TASK-1298  f95b30853e   5199 passed, 0 failed

#2006 — F1 and F2 both fixed.

F1: `resolved_reply_id` was seeded with the RAW user string and the reply
resolution sat in an ELSE-IF, so `--thread X --in-reply-to Y` took the thread
branch and wrote Y unvalidated. Resolution hoisted out of the branch; threading
still prefers an explicit --thread. Two tests, deliberately paired: one asserts
refusal with --thread present, the other asserts a VALID target still resolves to
the full parent id while --thread decides threading. Without the second, the fix
could pass by refusing whenever both flags appear.

F2: typed `MailboxResolveFailure { NotFound, AmbiguousPrefix }` read with
downcast_ref, following the crate's existing pattern (SoftSignpostShown,
MergeHoldRefusal, RebaseFailureExit) so all eight `?` callers are unchanged.
Display text is byte-identical — nothing user-facing moved; what changed is that
nothing DEPENDS on it.

THE FALSIFICATION FOR F2 IS THE ONE THAT DEMONSTRATES THE PROPERTY:

    reword the bail message, TYPED match    passes
    reword the bail message, PROSE match    RED
    restored                                passes

That is the finding's own test — "do not fix it by freezing the message" — run
rather than asserted.

#2014 — F1: `Unsupported` now yields Warn, a real measurement failure still
Fails. Extracted as a PURE classifier precisely because you flagged that
Linux-only CI structurally cannot see a Windows behaviour; the test exercises
the classifier directly, so Linux CI guards a Windows defect.

Falsified BOTH directions, and the second is the one I would not have thought to
run a week ago:

    blanket Err -> Fail    RED   (the original defect)
    blanket Err -> Warn    RED   (a fix that satisfies Windows and disables the
                                  check everywhere else)

TWO SELF-REPAIRS RECORDED IN THE COMMITS rather than quietly fixed: my #2014 test
initially absorbed four assertions from the neighbouring thresholds test (caught
by an out-of-scope binding), and my #2006 union earlier tonight carried an unused
import. Both are in the commit messages because the next person editing those
files will hit the same shapes.

ON F5: taken without defence and written into the #2006 commit. The prose match
sat four lines above the conflict I resolved two hours ago; I opened the file,
reasoned about its semantics, and read past it because attention was scoped to
the conflict markers. Recorded so the next conflict-resolver in that file knows
the scoping happens.

Nothing else assigned. Both PRs have CI running.
subject: #2006 and #2014 both done — F2's falsification runs the finding's own test (reword the message: typed passes, prose fails)
